melting_endothermic.name: Melting (Solid to Liquid)
melting_endothermic.description: Endothermic phase transition in which a solid absorbs thermal energy, increasing particle kinetic energy until particles overcome their fixed lattice positions to form a liquid.

intermolecular_forces.name: Strong Intermolecular Lattice Forces
intermolecular_forces.description: Strong electrostatic forces of attraction holding particles closely packed in fixed equilibrium positions within the solid crystalline lattice.

solid_lattice.name: Solid State (Regular Crystalline Lattice)
solid_lattice.description: Particles are closely packed in a regular, fixed geometric lattice with minimal spaces between them and vibrate only about fixed positions.

freezing_solidification.name: Freezing / Solidification (Liquid to Solid)
freezing_solidification.description: Exothermic phase transition in which a liquid loses thermal energy, slowing particle movement until strong attractive forces lock particles into a fixed solid lattice.

evaporation_boiling.name: Evaporation / Boiling (Liquid to Gas)
evaporation_boiling.description: Endothermic phase transition in which liquid particles gain sufficient kinetic energy to completely overcome intermolecular attractions and escape into the gas phase.

gas_dispersed.name: Gas State (Widely Spaced High-Speed Particles)
gas_dispersed.description: Particles are very far apart with negligible intermolecular forces, moving rapidly and randomly in all directions while colliding elastically with the container walls.

empty_vacuum_space.name: Large Intermolecular Empty Spaces
empty_vacuum_space.description: Large empty spaces between widely dispersed gas particles that allow gases to be easily compressed under applied pressure.

liquid_cluster.name: Liquid State (Disordered Close-Packed Particles)
liquid_cluster.description: Particles remain closely packed with small spaces between them but are disorderly arranged and can slide past one another to take the shape of their container.

condensation_exothermic.name: Condensation (Gas to Liquid)
condensation_exothermic.description: Exothermic phase transition in which gas particles lose kinetic energy upon cooling and are drawn together by attractive forces to form a liquid.
